title: Checkpoint: Superpower and Civil Rights
objective: After this level you can explain how the Cold War and the civil rights movement reshaped American life and rights between 1945 and 1975.
summary: In 1952 the Justice Department warned that segregation fed Communist propaganda. A timeline from 1947 to 1974 ties the Cold War and civil rights into one story.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 finale: in 1952, segregation became a Cold War problem.
cards.body: That year the Justice Department warned the Supreme Court that segregation was handing the Soviets propaganda. The Cold War and the civil rights movement were one story. Let’s line it up.

cards.headline: From the Truman Doctrine to a resignation

events.label: Truman asks Congress to aid Greece and Turkey
Brown v. Board rules segregated schools unequal
A new immigration law ends national quotas

cards.headline: Freedom at home, a weapon abroad
cards.body: In 1952 the Justice Department told the Court in the Brown case that “racial discrimination furnishes grist for the Communist propaganda mills.” Those same years brought suburbs for some and redlining for others, a march for jobs and freedom, a war that divided the country, and a scandal that ended with a president resigning. Read the timeline again: the rivalry abroad and the struggle for rights at home ran side by side, year after year.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 complete
learned: How the Cold War shaped American life, from Korea and the Red Scare to the race to the Moon.
How lawyers, students and marchers used courts and nonviolence to break down legal segregation.
Why Vietnam divided Americans, and how Watergate changed the way presidents are watched.
Who won new rights by 1975, from women and farmworkers to Native nations and new immigrants.

questions.prompt: Superpower and Civil Rights: which order of events is right?

options.label: Brown v. Board, the Truman Doctrine, Nixon resigns
options.rationale: The Truman Doctrine (1947) came before Brown (1954).

options.label: The Truman Doctrine, Brown v. Board, Nixon resigns
The Truman Doctrine, Nixon resigns, Brown v. Board
Nixon resigns, Brown v. Board, the Truman Doctrine

questions.explanation: The Truman Doctrine came in 1947, Brown in 1954 and Nixon’s resignation in 1974.

questions.prompt: What did the Justice Department warn the Court about in the Brown case in 1952?

options.label: That integration would weaken the army
options.rationale: The brief argued the opposite concern: discrimination hurt the US.

options.label: That the space race needed more schools
That the ruling would slow the Korean War
options.rationale: The level ties the brief to propaganda, not Korea.

options.label: That racial discrimination fed Communist propaganda

questions.explanation: The brief warned that “racial discrimination furnishes grist for the Communist propaganda mills.”

questions.prompt: Why might a Cold War official who cared most about containment still want segregation to end?

options.label: Segregation fed Soviet propaganda against the US
Segregation made the Moon landing more expensive
options.rationale: The level makes no link between segregation and NASA’s costs.

options.label: Ending it would end the military draft
Ending it would repeal the 1924 quotas
options.rationale: The quotas ended by a separate law in 1965.

questions.explanation: The 1952 brief warned that discrimination handed the Soviets propaganda, hurting the US in the rivalry containment was fighting.

questions.prompt: About how many people joined the March on Washington in 1963?

options.label: About 2,500
About 25,000
options.rationale: The crowd was about ten times bigger.

options.label: About 250,000
About 2.5 million

questions.explanation: About 250,000 people joined the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom.

questions.prompt: Brown ruled separate schools “inherently unequal.” Which earlier ruling from Level 67 had allowed segregation if facilities were “equal”?

options.label: Worcester v. Georgia
options.rationale: That 1832 case was about the Cherokee Nation.

options.label: Dred Scott v. Sandford
United States v. Nixon
options.rationale: That 1974 case was about the Watergate tapes.

options.label: Plessy v. Ferguson

questions.explanation: Plessy v. Ferguson (1896) allowed segregation if facilities were “equal”; Brown rejected that for schools.
